actual_src.headline: UK economy grew 0.1% in August, beating expectations

AUD|Employment Change.short: Shows Australian job growth, driving RBA interest rate expectations and the Australian dollar.
AUD|Employment Change.what: It measures the monthly change in the number of employed people in Australia. A higher reading indicates robust labor market growth.
AUD|Employment Change.why: Strong job gains pressure the RBA to hike rates, boosting the Australian dollar and moving local bond yields.
AUD|Employment Change.watch: Watch the split between full-time and part-time jobs, as full-time employment signals higher quality economic momentum.

AUD|Unemployment Rate.short: Tracks labor market slack in Australia, guiding RBA monetary policy and currency direction.
AUD|Unemployment Rate.what: It measures the percentage of the total workforce that is actively seeking employment and unemployed in Australia.
AUD|Unemployment Rate.why: A falling rate signals labor tightness and potential wage inflation, supporting the Australian dollar and yields.
AUD|Unemployment Rate.watch: Watch the participation rate alongside the headline figure, as a rising participation rate can mask job creation.

EUR|ECB President Lagarde Speaks.short: Provides direct insight into European Central Bank policy direction and future interest rate moves.
EUR|ECB President Lagarde Speaks.what: It captures public remarks and Q&A sessions by the President of the European Central Bank.
EUR|ECB President Lagarde Speaks.why: Traders listen for hints on rate cuts or hikes, directly driving the euro, European bond yields, and regional equities.
EUR|ECB President Lagarde Speaks.watch: Watch for subtle shifts in tone regarding inflation persistence and economic growth risks.

EUR|EU Economic Summit.short: Highlights political and fiscal coordination across the eurozone, impacting the euro and regional debt.
EUR|EU Economic Summit.what: It features meetings of European Union leaders discussing fiscal policy, structural reforms, and geopolitical challenges.
EUR|EU Economic Summit.why: Major policy agreements or disputes can trigger volatility in the euro and peripheral bond spreads.
EUR|EU Economic Summit.watch: Watch for joint fiscal initiatives, budget enforcement agreements, and responses to energy or security crises.

GBP|BOE Gov Bailey Speaks.short: Signals Bank of England policy intentions, heavily moving the British pound and UK gilts.
GBP|BOE Gov Bailey Speaks.what: It captures public commentary by the Governor of the Bank of England on the UK economy and monetary policy.
GBP|BOE Gov Bailey Speaks.why: Markets parse these speeches for clues on the timing of interest rate changes, directly moving sterling and gilt yields.
GBP|BOE Gov Bailey Speaks.watch: Watch for commentary on domestic wage growth, services inflation, and the balance of growth risks.

GBP|GDP m/m.short: Measures monthly UK economic momentum, moving the British pound and domestic equities.
GBP|GDP m/m.what: It measures the total value of goods and services produced in the UK compared to the previous month.
GBP|GDP m/m.why: Stronger growth supports the British pound and signals economic resilience, while contraction raises recession fears.
GBP|GDP m/m.watch: Watch the performance of the dominant services sector, as well as industrial production and construction output.

USD|CPI m/m.short: Gauges monthly US consumer inflation, driving Fed rate bets across bonds and the dollar.
USD|CPI m/m.what: It measures the monthly percentage change in the price of a basket of consumer goods and services.
USD|CPI m/m.why: Higher inflation erodes purchasing power and forces the Fed to keep rates high, boosting the US dollar and yields.
USD|CPI m/m.watch: Watch energy and food components, which can cause short-term volatility in the headline number.

USD|CPI y/y.short: Tracks annual US consumer inflation trends, shaping long-term Federal Reserve policy expectations.
USD|CPI y/y.what: It measures the percentage change in consumer prices over the past twelve months.
USD|CPI y/y.why: Persistent annual inflation keeps pressure on the Fed, impacting US Treasury yields, equity valuations, and the dollar.
USD|CPI y/y.watch: Watch how the reading compares to the Fed's 2% target and whether inflation is accelerating or decelerating.

USD|Core CPI m/m.short: Measures underlying US inflation excluding food and energy, heavily influencing Fed policy.
USD|Core CPI m/m.what: It tracks the monthly price change of goods and services consumed by households, excluding volatile food and energy.
USD|Core CPI m/m.why: Because it shows persistent inflation trends, a higher print strengthens the dollar and pushes yields higher.
USD|Core CPI m/m.watch: Watch the shelter and services components, which are often the stickiest parts of core inflation.

USD|Core CPI y/y.short: The Fed's preferred inflation trend gauge, driving global bond markets and currency values.
USD|Core CPI y/y.what: It measures the annual change in consumer prices excluding volatile food and energy categories.
USD|Core CPI y/y.why: It is a primary benchmark for underlying inflationary pressures, directly moving US yields, gold, and the US dollar.
USD|Core CPI y/y.watch: Watch shelter inflation trends and owner's equivalent rent for signs of lasting moderation.

USD|Core PPI m/m.short: Tracks wholesale input costs excluding food and energy, signaling future consumer price trends.
USD|Core PPI m/m.what: It measures the monthly change in prices received by producers, excluding volatile food, energy, and trade services.
USD|Core PPI m/m.why: Rising wholesale costs often filter down to consumers, influencing Fed policy expectations and moving the US dollar.
USD|Core PPI m/m.watch: Watch intermediate demand and healthcare or portfolio management services components for pipeline pressures.

USD|Core Retail Sales m/m.short: Measures underlying US consumer spending by stripping out autos and gas, moving equities.
USD|Core Retail Sales m/m.what: It tracks monthly retail sales excluding automobile, gasoline, building material, and food service sales.
USD|Core Retail Sales m/m.why: This is a cleaner read on consumer health and discretionary demand, moving retail stocks and broader equities.
USD|Core Retail Sales m/m.watch: Watch online retail and non-store retailer sales, which represent modern consumer spending habits.

USD|Fed Chairman Warsh Speaks.short: Provides direct signals on US monetary policy and interest rate paths from central bank leadership.
USD|Fed Chairman Warsh Speaks.what: It captures public remarks and policy stances delivered by the Federal Reserve Chair.
USD|Fed Chairman Warsh Speaks.why: Markets look for shifts in the Fed reaction function, causing rapid moves in US Treasuries, equities, and the dollar.
USD|Fed Chairman Warsh Speaks.watch: Watch for comments regarding the balance sheet, labor market health, and tolerance for above-target inflation.

USD|PPI m/m.short: Measures changes in wholesale prices, offering an early indicator of consumer inflation pressures.
USD|PPI m/m.what: It measures the monthly percentage change in the selling prices received by domestic producers.
USD|PPI m/m.why: Higher producer prices can compress corporate profit margins or pass through to consumers, moving bonds and equities.
USD|PPI m/m.watch: Watch final demand goods versus final demand services to see where price pressures are originating.

USD|Philly Fed Manufacturing Index.short: Provides an early regional read on US manufacturing health, moving industrial stocks and yields.
USD|Philly Fed Manufacturing Index.what: It measures business sentiment and activity levels among manufacturers in the Philadelphia Federal Reserve district.
USD|Philly Fed Manufacturing Index.why: As an early monthly indicator, it can shift sentiment on broader US economic growth and manufacturing health.
USD|Philly Fed Manufacturing Index.watch: Watch the new orders and prices paid sub-indexes for leading signals on demand and cost pressures.

USD|Retail Sales m/m.short: Measures total US consumer spending, which drives the broader economy and equity markets.
USD|Retail Sales m/m.what: It measures the total monthly change in retail and food services sales unadjusted for inflation.
USD|Retail Sales m/m.why: Strong consumer spending supports economic growth and corporate earnings, while weak data sparks recession fears.
USD|Retail Sales m/m.watch: Watch control group sales, which feed directly into the calculation of personal consumption expenditures (PCE).

USD|Unemployment Claims.short: Tracks weekly US job losses, offering real-time insight into labor market health.
USD|Unemployment Claims.what: It measures the number of individuals who filed for state unemployment insurance for the first time.
USD|Unemployment Claims.why: A sudden spike signals economic cooling and potential Fed rate cuts, moving bonds, gold, and the US dollar.
USD|Unemployment Claims.watch: Watch continuing claims to see how easily laid-off workers are finding new employment.

EUR|French Flash Manufacturing PMI.short: Markets watch French factory health as an early gauge for the broader Eurozone economy.
EUR|French Flash Manufacturing PMI.what: Measures activity levels in France's manufacturing sector based on purchasing managers' surveys.
EUR|French Flash Manufacturing PMI.why: Weakness pressures the euro and European equities. Strong prints boost regional risk sentiment.
EUR|French Flash Manufacturing PMI.watch: Watch the new orders sub-index and overall employment trends for underlying momentum.

EUR|French Flash Services PMI.short: Tracks French service sector momentum to gauge domestic economic health.
EUR|French Flash Services PMI.what: Measures business activity in France's dominant service industries via survey data.
EUR|French Flash Services PMI.why: Influences the euro and European bond yields by signaling domestic demand shifts.
EUR|French Flash Services PMI.watch: Pay attention to input cost and output price sub-indices for inflation pressures.

EUR|German Flash Manufacturing PMI.short: Germany's factory PMI is a key health check for the entire Eurozone industrial base.
EUR|German Flash Manufacturing PMI.what: Measures manufacturing sector output, new orders, and employment in Germany.
EUR|German Flash Manufacturing PMI.why: A critical driver for the euro, German bunds, and European cyclical stocks.
EUR|German Flash Manufacturing PMI.watch: Focus on the export orders sub-index to gauge global manufacturing demand.

EUR|German Flash Services PMI.short: Signals domestic economic resilience in the Eurozone's largest economy.
EUR|German Flash Services PMI.what: Measures activity levels across German service sector businesses.
EUR|German Flash Services PMI.why: Moves the euro and European interest rate expectations by reflecting domestic consumer health.
EUR|German Flash Services PMI.watch: Watch for wage growth clues within the services employment and price components.

GBP|Average Earnings Index 3m/y.short: Wages drive sticky inflation, making this a top metric for Bank of England rate decisions.
GBP|Average Earnings Index 3m/y.what: Measures the annual growth rate in average employee wages, including bonuses, over a rolling three-month period.
GBP|Average Earnings Index 3m/y.why: Hot wage growth pushes up British pound exchange rates and gilt yields due to rate hike fears.
GBP|Average Earnings Index 3m/y.watch: Compare regular pay excluding bonuses against total pay to assess underlying wage momentum.

GBP|CPI y/y.short: The primary inflation gauge dictating the Bank of England's interest rate path.
GBP|CPI y/y.what: Measures the annual percentage change in the price of a standard basket of consumer goods and services.
GBP|CPI y/y.why: High readings strengthen the British pound and depress UK bond prices as rate cuts are priced out.
GBP|CPI y/y.watch: Watch core CPI and services inflation, which exclude volatile food and energy costs.

GBP|Flash Manufacturing PMI.short: Provides an early look at UK factory output and economic momentum.
GBP|Flash Manufacturing PMI.what: Measures business conditions and purchasing activity across UK manufacturing firms.
GBP|Flash Manufacturing PMI.why: Moves the British pound and UK equities by signaling near-term industrial trends.
GBP|Flash Manufacturing PMI.watch: Check supply chain delivery times and input prices for early inflationary bottlenecks.

GBP|Flash Services PMI.short: The most important timely indicator for the dominant UK services sector.
GBP|Flash Services PMI.what: Measures output and business sentiment across UK service providers.
GBP|Flash Services PMI.why: Directly impacts Bank of England policy expectations, moving the pound and gilt yields.
GBP|Flash Services PMI.watch: Watch new business inflows and price charged sub-indices for inflation trends.

GBP|Retail Sales m/m.short: Measures consumer spending power and retail health in the UK economy.
GBP|Retail Sales m/m.what: Tracks the monthly change in the sales volume of retail goods.
GBP|Retail Sales m/m.why: Weak sales weigh on the British pound and retail stocks, signaling slowing consumer demand.
GBP|Retail Sales m/m.watch: Compare headline sales against core sales, which exclude volatile automotive fuel.

USD|Flash Manufacturing PMI.short: An early monthly read on US industrial health and economic momentum.
USD|Flash Manufacturing PMI.what: Measures output, orders, and employment in the US manufacturing sector.
USD|Flash Manufacturing PMI.why: Shifts US Treasury yields and the US dollar by signaling broader economic strength.
USD|Flash Manufacturing PMI.watch: Look at the employment and new orders components for future direction.

USD|Flash Services PMI.short: Crucial gauge of US service sector activity, which drives the broader economy.
USD|Flash Services PMI.what: Measures business activity across US service providers.
USD|Flash Services PMI.why: Moves the US dollar and bond markets by reflecting domestic economic resilience.
USD|Flash Services PMI.watch: Monitor the prices-charged component for clues on persistent service inflation.

USD|Revised UoM Consumer Sentiment.short: Confirms how optimistic American consumers feel about their financial futures.
USD|Revised UoM Consumer Sentiment.what: Measures consumer attitudes regarding personal finances and business conditions.
USD|Revised UoM Consumer Sentiment.why: Influences consumer discretionary stocks and the US dollar based on expected spending.
USD|Revised UoM Consumer Sentiment.watch: Check for notable revisions from the preliminary reading to gauge sentiment stability.

USD|Revised UoM Inflation Expectations.short: Monitors what consumers expect inflation to do, influencing Fed policy choices.
USD|Revised UoM Inflation Expectations.what: Measures long-term and one-year consumer inflation expectations from the UoM survey.
USD|Revised UoM Inflation Expectations.why: Higher expectations can trigger Fed rate hike fears, lifting the US dollar and Treasury yields.
USD|Revised UoM Inflation Expectations.watch: Focus specifically on the five-year-ahead inflation expectation gauge, which the Fed closely monitors.

AUD|Flash Manufacturing PMI.short: Gauges factory sector health to signal broader Australian economic momentum and move the AUD.
AUD|Flash Manufacturing PMI.what: It measures manufacturing activity based on surveys of purchasing managers. A reading above 50 indicates expansion.
AUD|Flash Manufacturing PMI.why: Markets watch it for early signs of economic growth or slowdown, directly impacting the Australian dollar and local rate expectations.
AUD|Flash Manufacturing PMI.watch: Pay attention to the new orders and employment sub-indices for future momentum.

AUD|Flash Services PMI.short: Tracks dominant services sector activity to gauge domestic economic health and influence rate bets.
AUD|Flash Services PMI.what: It measures business conditions in the services sector via monthly purchasing manager surveys. Services make up the bulk of Australia's GDP.
AUD|Flash Services PMI.why: Stronger readings boost the AUD and rate hike expectations, while contractions pressure the currency.
AUD|Flash Services PMI.watch: Look at the input and output prices sub-components for underlying inflation pressures.

AUD|RBA Assist Gov Kent Speaks.short: Provides clues on central bank policy direction, directly impacting Australian bond yields and the AUD.
AUD|RBA Assist Gov Kent Speaks.what: Speeches by central bank officials often outline current economic assessments and future monetary policy leanings.
AUD|RBA Assist Gov Kent Speaks.why: Traders listen for hints about upcoming rate hikes or cuts, moving the Australian dollar and short-term interest rate futures.
AUD|RBA Assist Gov Kent Speaks.watch: Watch for any direct comments on inflation targets or employment thresholds.

AUD|RBA Deputy Gov Hauser Speaks.short: Offers insight into central bank thinking, swaying Australian dollar and bond market pricing.
AUD|RBA Deputy Gov Hauser Speaks.what: Public remarks by the Deputy Governor detailing the central bank's perspective on economic risks and policy.
AUD|RBA Deputy Gov Hauser Speaks.why: Hawkish or dovish shifts in tone can rapidly reprice Australian interest rate expectations and move currency pairs.
AUD|RBA Deputy Gov Hauser Speaks.watch: Note any divergence from consensus views on economic growth or inflation persistence.

All|IMF Meetings.short: Global economic policy summits that shape sovereign debt discussions and broader market sentiment.
All|IMF Meetings.what: Gatherings of global central bankers, finance ministers, and economists discussing macroeconomic stability and forecasts.
All|IMF Meetings.why: Official statements and policy panels can trigger shifts in global risk sentiment, emerging market assets, and major currencies.
All|IMF Meetings.watch: Watch for updated global growth forecasts and commentary on international trade or debt issues.

CAD|BOC Business Outlook Survey.short: Measures corporate sentiment in Canada to predict future business investment, hiring, and inflation trends.
CAD|BOC Business Outlook Survey.what: A direct survey of Canadian businesses regarding their future sales expectations, hiring plans, and capacity pressures.
CAD|BOC Business Outlook Survey.why: The Bank of Canada heavily relies on this survey to set monetary policy, making it a key driver for the Canadian dollar.
CAD|BOC Business Outlook Survey.watch: Focus on indicators regarding corporate pricing behavior and labour shortages.

CAD|CPI m/m.short: Measures monthly consumer inflation changes to drive Bank of Canada rate decisions and the loonie.
CAD|CPI m/m.what: Tracks the month-over-month change in the price of a standard basket of goods and services purchased by consumers.
CAD|CPI m/m.why: Higher-than-expected inflation increases the odds of Bank of Canada interest rate hikes, strengthening the Canadian dollar.
CAD|CPI m/m.watch: Look at the month-over-month percentage change and headline revisions.

CAD|Common CPI y/y.short: Tracks trend inflation by excluding volatile items, helping the Bank of Canada gauge underlying price pressures.
CAD|Common CPI y/y.what: A Bank of Canada preferred core inflation measure that tracks common price changes across various CPI components.
CAD|Common CPI y/y.why: Persistent readings above target keep interest rates elevated, supporting Canadian bond yields and the currency.
CAD|Common CPI y/y.watch: Compare the print against the Bank of Canada's target inflation band.

CAD|Core CPI m/m.short: Strips out volatile items to reveal core monthly inflation trends, influencing Canadian interest rate expectations.
CAD|Core CPI m/m.what: Measures monthly price changes in consumer goods excluding volatile categories like food and energy.
CAD|Core CPI m/m.why: Markets use this measure to gauge persistent domestic inflation pressures that dictate central bank policy.
CAD|Core CPI m/m.watch: Check for momentum shifts in service sector price components.

CAD|Core Retail Sales m/m.short: Gauges consumer spending momentum excluding autos, driving Canadian economic growth expectations.
CAD|Core Retail Sales m/m.what: Measures the monthly change in retail sales receipts, stripping out volatile automobile purchases.
CAD|Core Retail Sales m/m.why: Robust consumer spending supports GDP growth and can boost the Canadian dollar if it exceeds forecasts.
CAD|Core Retail Sales m/m.watch: Examine volume versus value figures to separate real growth from pure price inflation.

CAD|IPPI m/m.short: Tracks upstream factory gate inflation to signal future consumer price pressures and manufacturing health.
CAD|IPPI m/m.what: Measures the change in prices received by Canadian manufacturers for their output.
CAD|IPPI m/m.why: Acts as an early indicator of downstream consumer inflation and affects the valuation of the Canadian dollar.
CAD|IPPI m/m.watch: Focus on commodity price components within the manufacturing chain.

CAD|Median CPI y/y.short: Measures the middle price change across all CPI components to provide a clear view of underlying inflation.
CAD|Median CPI y/y.what: A primary Bank of Canada core inflation metric that isolates the median rate of price change across categories.
CAD|Median CPI y/y.why: Persistent core readings guide central bank rate paths, influencing Canadian fixed income and currency markets.
CAD|Median CPI y/y.watch: Watch whether the reading stays stubborn or trends back toward the 2% midpoint.

CAD|NHPI m/m.short: Tracks new home price changes to gauge Canadian real estate market health and consumer wealth effects.
CAD|NHPI m/m.what: Measures the monthly change in residential house prices charged to builders and buyers.
CAD|NHPI m/m.why: Property market health affects domestic consumption, mortgage credit growth, and Canadian bank stocks.
CAD|NHPI m/m.watch: Look for regional divergences, particularly in major housing hubs like Toronto and Vancouver.

CAD|RMPI m/m.short: Measures raw material costs for industries, serving as an early warning for broader inflation trends.
CAD|RMPI m/m.what: Tracks the monthly change in prices paid by Canadian manufacturers for raw materials and commodities.
CAD|RMPI m/m.why: Spikes in raw material costs often feed into producer and consumer prices, swaying inflation expectations and currency value.
CAD|RMPI m/m.watch: Pay close attention to energy and metal price sub-components.

CAD|Retail Sales m/m.short: Measures total consumer purchasing power to gauge immediate Canadian economic growth and demand.
CAD|Retail Sales m/m.what: Tracks the total monthly value of retail goods sold across brick-and-mortar and online stores.
CAD|Retail Sales m/m.why: Stronger consumer spending signals a healthy domestic economy, supporting the Canadian dollar and retail stocks.
CAD|Retail Sales m/m.watch: Compare headline numbers against core numbers to filter out the impact of volatile auto sales.

CAD|Trimmed CPI y/y.short: Removes extreme price shifts to reveal persistent underlying Canadian inflation trends.
CAD|Trimmed CPI y/y.what: A core inflation measure that excludes the most volatile 20% of CPI component price changes each month.
CAD|Trimmed CPI y/y.why: Closely monitored by the Bank of Canada to set monetary policy, directly impacting Canadian bond and currency markets.
CAD|Trimmed CPI y/y.watch: Check the spread between trimmed inflation and the headline CPI figure.

CHF|Summary of Monetary Policy Discussio.short: Reveals Swiss National Bank policy debates, guiding franc valuation and local bond yields.
CHF|Summary of Monetary Policy Discussio.what: Publishes detailed insights from the Swiss National Bank's rate-setting meetings and economic debates.
CHF|Summary of Monetary Policy Discussio.why: Traders analyze the text for hints on future interest rate moves and currency intervention stances, moving the Swiss franc.
CHF|Summary of Monetary Policy Discussio.watch: Look for explicit comments regarding exchange rate valuations or inflation risks.

CNY|1-y Loan Prime Rate.short: Sets the benchmark for corporate and household loans in China, moving global commodity and equity markets.
CNY|1-y Loan Prime Rate.what: The benchmark interest rate used by commercial banks for most general loans and corporate lending in China.
CNY|1-y Loan Prime Rate.why: Cuts signal monetary easing to support growth, often boosting emerging markets and commodity-linked currencies.
CNY|1-y Loan Prime Rate.watch: Watch for alignment with previous cuts in the medium-term lending facility rate.

CNY|5-y Loan Prime Rate.short: Drives Chinese mortgage pricing and property sector sentiment, impacting global growth and industrial metals.
CNY|5-y Loan Prime Rate.what: The benchmark interest rate for long-term loans, particularly mortgages, in China's financial system.
CNY|5-y Loan Prime Rate.why: Reductions aim to stabilize the struggling property market, influencing industrial metal prices and global risk sentiment.
CNY|5-y Loan Prime Rate.watch: Assess the magnitude of any cuts and their potential impact on homebuyer demand.

CNY|Fixed Asset Investment ytd/y.short: Tracks capital spending in China to gauge infrastructure and industrial expansion momentum.
CNY|Fixed Asset Investment ytd/y.what: Measures the year-to-date change in capital investments across real estate, infrastructure, and manufacturing.
CNY|Fixed Asset Investment ytd/y.why: Strong investment data supports global industrial commodity demand, such as copper and iron ore.
CNY|Fixed Asset Investment ytd/y.watch: Compare real estate investment growth versus state-backed infrastructure spending.

CNY|Foreign Direct Investment ytd/y.short: Gauges foreign corporate confidence in China's economy, influencing broader emerging market sentiment.
CNY|Foreign Direct Investment ytd/y.what: Tracks year-to-date capital inflows from foreign entities into Chinese business operations and projects.
CNY|Foreign Direct Investment ytd/y.why: Declining or rising FDI trends reflect global corporate sentiment toward operating in China.
CNY|Foreign Direct Investment ytd/y.watch: Check sector breakdowns to see where foreign capital is concentrating.

CNY|GDP q/y.short: Measures China's overall economic growth pace, setting the tone for global demand and commodity markets.
CNY|GDP q/y.what: Calculates the total quarterly economic output growth rate for the world's second-largest economy.
CNY|GDP q/y.why: Misses or beats relative to official targets impact global equities, emerging markets, and industrial commodities.
CNY|GDP q/y.watch: Look at the year-over-year versus quarter-over-quarter prints and industrial sector contributions.

CNY|Industrial Production y/y.short: Tracks factory output in China to signal manufacturing health and global supply chain demand.
CNY|Industrial Production y/y.what: Measures the year-over-year output change of Chinese factories, mines, and utilities.
CNY|Industrial Production y/y.why: Key driver for global commodity prices and equities tied to Chinese industrial demand.
CNY|Industrial Production y/y.watch: Review sub-sectors like high-tech manufacturing versus traditional heavy industry.

CNY|NBS Press Conference.short: Provides official color on Chinese economic data releases, shaping near-term market expectations.
CNY|NBS Press Conference.what: Press briefing by the National Bureau of Statistics detailing macroeconomic data and policy outlooks.
CNY|NBS Press Conference.why: Official commentary can alter market interpretations of recent growth data and sway regional asset prices.
CNY|NBS Press Conference.watch: Listen for explicit government targets or hints regarding upcoming fiscal stimulus.

CNY|New Home Prices m/m.short: Measures Chinese real estate price momentum to gauge property sector health and consumer confidence.
CNY|New Home Prices m/m.what: Tracks the monthly price changes of new residential properties across major Chinese cities.
CNY|New Home Prices m/m.why: Stabilizing property prices are crucial for restoring consumer confidence and supporting broader economic growth.
CNY|New Home Prices m/m.watch: Look at price trends in Tier 1 cities versus smaller Tier 2 and 3 cities.

CNY|Retail Sales y/y.short: Measures Chinese consumer spending, driving global growth expectations and commodities.
CNY|Retail Sales y/y.what: It tracks the year-over-year percentage change in total receipts of retail goods and services in China.
CNY|Retail Sales y/y.why: It dictates demand for industrial metals and equities, directly moving the Australian dollar and copper.
CNY|Retail Sales y/y.watch: Look for catering versus goods sales and momentum in online retail.

CNY|Unemployment Rate.short: Gauges China's labor market health and potential for policy intervention.
CNY|Unemployment Rate.what: It measures the percentage of the total workforce that is actively seeking employment in urban areas.
CNY|Unemployment Rate.why: High joblessness risks lower consumer spending and triggers monetary stimulus, impacting Asian equities and industrial commodities.
CNY|Unemployment Rate.watch: Focus on youth unemployment figures and urban survey details.

EUR|Belgian NBB Business Climate.short: Early indicator of Eurozone industrial sentiment and economic direction.
EUR|Belgian NBB Business Climate.what: It measures manufacturing executives' business confidence regarding demand, stocks, and production.
EUR|Belgian NBB Business Climate.why: As an early reporter, it helps forecast broader Eurozone GDP and moves the euro and European stocks.
EUR|Belgian NBB Business Climate.watch: Check the manufacturing sub-components for unexpected turning points.

EUR|Consumer Confidence.short: Tracks household sentiment to gauge future Eurozone consumer spending.
EUR|Consumer Confidence.what: It measures consumers' assessment of their financial situation and the broader economic outlook.
EUR|Consumer Confidence.why: Stronger confidence supports retail stocks and the euro, while pessimism signals weak domestic demand.
EUR|Consumer Confidence.watch: Look at major components like households' intentions for major purchases.

EUR|Current Account.short: Measures Eurozone trade and investment flows with the rest of the world.
EUR|Current Account.what: It records the net flow of goods, services, and investment income between the Eurozone and foreign economies.
EUR|Current Account.why: A large surplus supports the euro's fundamental value against major currencies.
EUR|Current Account.watch: Distinguish between the trade surplus and net income transfers.

EUR|Flash Manufacturing PMI.short: Timely gauge of Eurozone industrial health, moving the euro and regional equities.
EUR|Flash Manufacturing PMI.what: It surveys purchasing managers on factory output, new orders, and employment.
EUR|Flash Manufacturing PMI.why: It acts as a leading growth indicator, directly impacting the euro and cyclical European stocks.
EUR|Flash Manufacturing PMI.watch: Watch the new orders-to-inventory ratio and output price sub-indices.

EUR|Flash Services PMI.short: Measures activity in the dominant Eurozone services sector.
EUR|Flash Services PMI.what: It tracks sentiment among service-sector managers regarding business activity and demand.
EUR|Flash Services PMI.why: Services drive domestic inflation and growth, making this crucial for European Central Bank rate expectations and the euro.
EUR|Flash Services PMI.watch: Pay close attention to input and output price trends for inflation clues.

EUR|German Buba Monthly Report.short: Provides detailed Bundesbank economic analysis and German policy outlooks.
EUR|German Buba Monthly Report.what: It publishes deep-dive economic data, forecasts, and essays from Germany's central bank.
EUR|German Buba Monthly Report.why: It often reveals the ECB policy stance of the hawkish German block, moving German bunds and the euro.
EUR|German Buba Monthly Report.watch: Look for shifts in inflation assessments and economic growth risks.

EUR|German Buba President Nagel Speaks.short: Signals potential European Central Bank policy bias and German economic views.
EUR|German Buba President Nagel Speaks.what: Bundesbank President Nagel delivers public remarks on monetary policy and economic conditions.
EUR|German Buba President Nagel Speaks.why: His influential hawkish voice can quickly shift interest rate expectations, European bond yields, and the euro.
EUR|German Buba President Nagel Speaks.watch: Listen for comments regarding inflation persistence and rate cut paths.

EUR|German PPI m/m.short: Early upstream inflation gauge for Europe's largest economy.
EUR|German PPI m/m.what: It measures the monthly price change of goods sold by German manufacturers.
EUR|German PPI m/m.why: Upstream price pressures eventually feed into consumer inflation, moving German bunds and the euro.
EUR|German PPI m/m.watch: Focus on energy and intermediate goods prices for signs of persistent cost pressures.

EUR|German ZEW Economic Sentiment.short: Measures institutional investor optimism for the German economy.
EUR|German ZEW Economic Sentiment.what: It surveys financial analysts and institutional investors on six-month economic expectations.
EUR|German ZEW Economic Sentiment.why: It serves as a leading indicator for Eurozone economic trends, impacting German DAX and the euro.
EUR|German ZEW Economic Sentiment.watch: Compare the current situation index with the future expectations index.

EUR|ZEW Economic Sentiment.short: Gauges institutional investor confidence in the broader Eurozone economy.
EUR|ZEW Economic Sentiment.what: It measures economic expectations over a six-month horizon among financial experts.
EUR|ZEW Economic Sentiment.why: It provides early signals for Eurozone business cycles, moving European equities and the euro.
EUR|ZEW Economic Sentiment.watch: Look for divergence between German sentiment and the aggregate Eurozone reading.

GBP|10-y Bond Auction.short: Tests investor demand and pricing for UK long-term sovereign debt.
GBP|10-y Bond Auction.what: The UK Debt Management Office sells 10-year gilts to institutional investors.
GBP|10-y Bond Auction.why: Poor demand or high yields signal fiscal anxiety, moving gilt prices and the British pound.
GBP|10-y Bond Auction.watch: Watch the bid-to-cover ratio and the tail between average and accepted yields.

GBP|CBI Industrial Order Expectations.short: Measures order book strength for UK manufacturers.
GBP|CBI Industrial Order Expectations.what: It tracks the balance of manufacturers reporting above- or below-normal order books.
GBP|CBI Industrial Order Expectations.why: It helps forecast UK industrial production and GDP, impacting the British pound and industrial stocks.
GBP|CBI Industrial Order Expectations.watch: Watch export order sub-indices for global demand trends.

GBP|Claimant Count Change.short: Timely indicator of UK labor market slack and jobless claims.
GBP|Claimant Count Change.what: It measures the monthly change in people claiming unemployment-related benefits.
GBP|Claimant Count Change.why: Rising claims signal a cooling labor market, shifting Bank of England rate expectations and sterling.
GBP|Claimant Count Change.watch: Check for revisions to prior months and alignment with the ILO unemployment rate.

GBP|Core CPI y/y.short: Measures underlying UK inflation excluding volatile food and energy.
GBP|Core CPI y/y.what: It tracks the annual price change of a subset of consumer goods excluding food, energy, alcohol, and tobacco.
GBP|Core CPI y/y.why: This is the primary metric the Bank of England watches for domestic inflation persistence, moving gilts and the pound.
GBP|Core CPI y/y.watch: Focus on services inflation components within the broader report.

GBP|GfK Consumer Confidence.short: Tracks UK consumer optimism regarding personal finances and the economy.
GBP|GfK Consumer Confidence.what: It surveys consumers on their financial situation, major purchases, and economic outlook.
GBP|GfK Consumer Confidence.why: It influences retail stocks and consumer discretionary sectors, impacting the British pound.
GBP|GfK Consumer Confidence.watch: Check major purchases and personal financial outlook sub-indices.

GBP|HPI y/y.short: Measures annual house price inflation across the United Kingdom.
GBP|HPI y/y.what: It tracks the percentage change in residential property prices using official transactions.
GBP|HPI y/y.why: Housing wealth affects consumer spending and bank mortgage portfolios, moving UK banks and sterling.
GBP|HPI y/y.watch: Look for regional divergences and transaction volume trends.

GBP|MPC Member Greene Speaks.short: Provides insight into Bank of England policy voting intentions.
GBP|MPC Member Greene Speaks.what: MPC member Megan Greene delivers public remarks on the UK economy and monetary policy.
GBP|MPC Member Greene Speaks.why: Hawkish or dovish shifts can alter rate cut expectations, directly moving gilts and the British pound.
GBP|MPC Member Greene Speaks.watch: Listen for specific views on wage growth and services inflation.

GBP|PPI Input m/m.short: Tracks raw material cost pressures for UK producers.
GBP|PPI Input m/m.what: It measures the monthly change in the price of materials and fuels purchased by UK manufacturers.
GBP|PPI Input m/m.why: It acts as a leading indicator for consumer price inflation, moving short-term gilts and sterling.
GBP|PPI Input m/m.watch: Pay attention to imported raw material and energy price changes.

GBP|PPI Output m/m.short: Measures factory gate inflation for UK manufactured goods.
GBP|PPI Output m/m.what: It tracks the monthly price change of goods leaving UK factory gates.
GBP|PPI Output m/m.why: It signals pass-through of input costs to finished goods, moving the British pound and gilt yields.
GBP|PPI Output m/m.watch: Focus on core output inflation excluding volatile food items.

GBP|Public Sector Net Borrowing.short: Measures the UK government's monthly fiscal deficit and debt issuance needs.
GBP|Public Sector Net Borrowing.what: It tracks the difference between public sector spending and revenues.
GBP|Public Sector Net Borrowing.why: High borrowing strains public finances, pressuring UK government bonds and the British pound.
GBP|Public Sector Net Borrowing.watch: Compare figures against official Office for Budget Responsibility forecasts.

GBP|RPI y/y.short: Legacy UK inflation measure including housing costs.
GBP|RPI y/y.what: It tracks annual price changes across a broad basket of goods, notably including mortgage interest and council tax.
GBP|RPI y/y.why: Though superseded by CPI, it is still used for index-linked gilts and rail fare hikes, moving bond markets.
GBP|RPI y/y.watch: Check the difference between RPI and CPI inflation rates.

GBP|Rightmove HPI m/m.short: Early indicator of UK property market asking prices.
GBP|Rightmove HPI m/m.what: It measures the monthly percentage change in asking prices on properties listed on Rightmove.
GBP|Rightmove HPI m/m.why: As a leading housing indicator, it affects homebuilder stocks and consumer sentiment regarding real estate.
GBP|Rightmove HPI m/m.watch: Look at newly marketed property prices versus seasonal trends.

GBP|Unemployment Rate.short: Measures the proportion of jobless workers actively seeking UK employment.
GBP|Unemployment Rate.what: It tracks the ILO unemployment rate among the active UK workforce.
GBP|Unemployment Rate.why: Labor market slack drives wage growth, heavily influencing Bank of England interest rate decisions and the pound.
GBP|Unemployment Rate.watch: Monitor wage growth and employment change figures released alongside it.

JPY|Flash Manufacturing PMI.short: Tracks early industrial health to gauge overall Japanese economic momentum and currency direction.
JPY|Flash Manufacturing PMI.what: It measures the overall health of the manufacturing sector based on survey data from purchasing managers.
JPY|Flash Manufacturing PMI.why: Markets watch this for early signals of economic growth, moving the Japanese Yen and domestic equities.
JPY|Flash Manufacturing PMI.watch: Pay close attention to the new orders and employment sub-components for underlying momentum.

JPY|National Core CPI y/y.short: Measures underlying inflation trends to guide Bank of Japan monetary policy and bond yields.
JPY|National Core CPI y/y.what: It tracks the year-over-year change in consumer prices nationwide, excluding volatile fresh food.
JPY|National Core CPI y/y.why: It drives Bank of Japan rate expectations, heavily influencing Japanese Government Bond yields and the Yen.
JPY|National Core CPI y/y.watch: Look at services inflation and the exclusion of energy to gauge domestic price pressures.

JPY|Tertiary Industry Activity m/m.short: Measures service sector output to gauge domestic demand and broader Japanese economic growth.
JPY|Tertiary Industry Activity m/m.what: It tracks the monthly change in output from service-oriented industries in Japan.
JPY|Tertiary Industry Activity m/m.why: Since services dominate Japan's GDP, this release moves the Yen and domestic consumer stocks.
JPY|Tertiary Industry Activity m/m.watch: Check retail, healthcare, and financial services sub-sectors for consumer strength.

JPY|Trade Balance.short: Tracks import and export trends to assess external demand and Yen valuation fundamentals.
JPY|Trade Balance.what: It measures the difference in value between exported and imported goods in Japan.
JPY|Trade Balance.why: It reflects global demand and impacts current account balances, moving the Japanese Yen.
JPY|Trade Balance.watch: Watch export volumes and automobile shipments alongside import costs driven by energy.

NZD|BusinessNZ Services Index.short: Measures service sector momentum to gauge New Zealand domestic economic health.
NZD|BusinessNZ Services Index.what: It tracks activity levels in New Zealand's services sector via monthly purchasing manager surveys.
NZD|BusinessNZ Services Index.why: Markets use it to assess domestic demand, impacting the New Zealand Dollar and interest rate expectations.
NZD|BusinessNZ Services Index.watch: Focus on the employment and new orders indices for forward-looking momentum.

NZD|CPI q/q.short: Tracks consumer price changes to drive Reserve Bank of New Zealand interest rate decisions.
NZD|CPI q/q.what: It measures the quarterly percentage change in the cost of a basket of consumer goods and services.
NZD|CPI q/q.why: It is the primary gauge for inflation, directly moving the New Zealand Dollar and wholesale interest rates.
NZD|CPI q/q.watch: Pay attention to non-tradeable inflation, which reflects domestic price pressures.

NZD|Credit Card Spending y/y.short: Offers a timely read on New Zealand consumer spending habits and domestic retail demand.
NZD|Credit Card Spending y/y.what: It tracks the year-over-year percentage change in total credit card spending.
NZD|Credit Card Spending y/y.why: It provides a quick proxy for retail sales and consumer confidence, influencing the New Zealand Dollar.
NZD|Credit Card Spending y/y.watch: Differentiate between retail spending and travel-related categories to gauge domestic resilience.

NZD|GDT Price Index.short: Measures dairy auction prices to gauge New Zealand export income and currency strength.
NZD|GDT Price Index.what: It tracks average prices achieved at global dairy trade auctions.
NZD|GDT Price Index.why: Dairy is New Zealand's top export, making this index a key driver for the New Zealand Dollar and terms of trade.
NZD|GDT Price Index.watch: Watch whole milk powder prices, as they carry the heaviest weight in the index.

NZD|Trade Balance.short: Measures export performance against imports to assess New Zealand's external economic balance.
NZD|Trade Balance.what: It tracks the net balance of goods and services exported versus imported by New Zealand.
NZD|Trade Balance.why: It impacts current account dynamics and influences New Zealand Dollar valuations.
NZD|Trade Balance.watch: Monitor export values for key commodities like dairy, meat, and forestry products.

USD|ADP Weekly Employment Change.short: Provides high-frequency payroll estimates to gauge US labor market health before official data.
USD|ADP Weekly Employment Change.what: It measures weekly changes in private sector employment based on payroll processing data.
USD|ADP Weekly Employment Change.why: Markets track it for early labor market signals, which can sway US Treasury yields and the US Dollar.
USD|ADP Weekly Employment Change.watch: Look for consistency with monthly non-farm payroll trends and prior week revisions.

USD|API Weekly Statistical Bulletin.short: Provides an early estimate of US oil inventories ahead of official government data.
USD|API Weekly Statistical Bulletin.what: It measures weekly changes in crude oil, gasoline, and distillate stockpiles.
USD|API Weekly Statistical Bulletin.why: It acts as a leading indicator for the official EIA report, moving crude oil futures.
USD|API Weekly Statistical Bulletin.watch: Compare crude inventory builds or draws with Cushing, Oklahoma storage levels.

USD|Building Permits.short: Acts as a leading indicator for US housing construction and future economic activity.
USD|Building Permits.what: It measures the number of new housing units authorized by building permits.
USD|Building Permits.why: It signals future construction activity, impacting homebuilder stocks and US Treasury yields.
USD|Building Permits.watch: Distinguish between single-family and multi-family permit trends for sector health.

USD|CB Leading Index m/m.short: Aggregates key indicators to forecast future economic direction and recession risks.
USD|CB Leading Index m/m.what: It combines ten economic components, including yields, factory orders, and permits, into a single index.
USD|CB Leading Index m/m.why: Markets watch it to gauge the medium-term economic outlook, affecting equities and bonds.
USD|CB Leading Index m/m.watch: Check which specific sub-components are driving the monthly change.

USD|Crude Oil Inventories.short: Measures weekly US commercial petroleum stocks to gauge supply and demand balance.
USD|Crude Oil Inventories.what: It tracks the change in barrels of commercial crude oil held in US storage tanks.
USD|Crude Oil Inventories.why: It directly influences global oil prices and energy sector equities.
USD|Crude Oil Inventories.watch: Pay attention to product inventories like gasoline and heating oil alongside crude.

USD|Housing Starts.short: Measures new residential construction to gauge immediate demand in the US housing sector.
USD|Housing Starts.what: It tracks the number of new residential construction projects that have begun during the month.
USD|Housing Starts.why: It reflects direct economic activity in housing, moving homebuilder equities and interest rates.
USD|Housing Starts.watch: Watch for regional divergences and single-family construction volumes.

USD|NAHB Housing Market Index.short: Gauges homebuilder confidence to assess the future health of the US housing market.
USD|NAHB Housing Market Index.what: It measures builder perceptions of current and future single-family home sales.
USD|NAHB Housing Market Index.why: It provides an early read on housing sector momentum, moving real estate stocks and housing-related assets.
USD|NAHB Housing Market Index.watch: Watch the traffic of prospective buyers sub-index for real demand signals.

USD|Natural Gas Storage.short: Tracks weekly underground natural gas inventories to price seasonal energy contracts.
USD|Natural Gas Storage.what: It measures the change in cubic feet of natural gas held in underground storage facilities.
USD|Natural Gas Storage.why: It dictates near-term supply balances, heavily moving natural gas futures and utility stocks.
USD|Natural Gas Storage.watch: Compare the reported storage change against seasonal averages and market consensus.

USD|Pending Home Sales m/m.short: Tracks signed contracts on existing homes to gauge future US housing market transactions.
USD|Pending Home Sales m/m.what: It measures the monthly change in contract activity for existing home sales.
USD|Pending Home Sales m/m.why: It acts as a leading indicator for existing home sales data, affecting real estate and broader consumer sectors.
USD|Pending Home Sales m/m.watch: Look at regional data to spot geographic trends in housing demand.
